name: Lais Ribeiro
milestone_by_age_26: Was the most-booked model at São Paulo Fashion Week in 2011 at age 21, walking 27 runway shows.
early_history_summary: Discovered through a modeling competition in her hometown around 2009, Ribeiro transitioned from nursing studies to modeling, quickly moving from local shows in Brazil to São Paulo Fashion Week and then to New York.
family_context_summary: Born in a small town in Piauí, Brazil to a modest family; was studying to become a nurse before a friend suggested she try modeling.
primary_early_advantage_tags: physical attributes, Brazilian model ecosystem, VS pipeline, modest background
evidence_summary: Ribeiro was discovered through a modeling competition in her hometown around 2009, transitioning from nursing studies to a modeling career. By 2011, she was the most-booked model at São Paulo Fashion Week with 27 runway shows, demonstrating rapid ascent in the fashion industry. She came from a modest background in small-town Brazil with no family connections to fashion or modeling. Her physical attributes (6'0 height) and the structural wave of Brazilian model dominance in the early 2010s were key advantages. A friend in the modeling industry provided her initial entry point.
starting_point: Born in a small town in Piauí, Brazil to a modest family; was training to become a nurse before a friend suggested she try modeling.
current_position: Victoria's Secret Angel and fashion model; married to former NBA player Joakim Noah; continues to model and resides in the United States.

trajectory.event: Walked in Rag and Bone Fall 2010 show, her first major modeling gig, and began working with Victoria's Secret.

Married former NBA player Joakim Noah.

name: Marco Fu
milestone_by_age_26: Won both the IBSF World Snooker Championship and the IBSF World Under-21 Snooker Championship in 1997 at age 19.
early_history_summary: Began playing snooker at age 9 in Hong Kong, migrated to Vancouver at age 12, and was invited back to Hong Kong at age 18 by the Billiard Sports Control Council to begin his professional career, winning world amateur titles before turning professional.
family_context_summary: Born in Hong Kong; family migrated to Vancouver, Canada when he was 12, providing a middle-class upbringing in a new country.
primary_early_advantage_tags: early specialization, snooker culture, HK billiard council support, migration
evidence_summary: Fu began playing snooker at age 9 in Hong Kong and migrated to Vancouver at 12, maintaining his interest in the sport. At 18, he was invited back to Hong Kong by the Billiard Sports Control Council to pursue professional snooker. He won both the IBSF World and World Under-21 Championships in 1997 at age 19, then turned professional and reached the Grand Prix final in his debut 1998 season. His family's migration to Canada provided a middle-class upbringing, and the Hong Kong snooker establishment actively supported his career development.
starting_point: Born in Hong Kong; family migrated to Vancouver, Canada when he was 12, providing a middle-class upbringing in a new country.
current_position: Professional snooker player on the World Snooker Tour; three-time ranking event winner; career-high world ranking No. 5; continues to compete.

name: Karin Balzer
milestone_by_age_26: Won silver in the 80m hurdles at the 1962 European Athletics Championships at age 24.
early_history_summary: Competed in track and field from her teens in Magdeburg, East Germany, qualifying for the 1960 Olympics at age 22 and winning her first international medal (silver) at the 1962 European Championships.
family_context_summary: Born Karin Richert in Magdeburg, East Germany; competed in track and field events from her teens in the East German sports system.
primary_early_advantage_tags: East German sports system, coach-husband, athletics pipeline, Stasi adversity
evidence_summary: Balzer competed in track and field from her teens in Magdeburg, East Germany, qualifying for the 1960 Olympics at age 22. She won silver at the 1962 European Championships and Olympic gold at the 1964 Tokyo Olympics at age 26. Her coach Karl-Heinz Balzer, whom she married in 1961, provided sustained individualized training. The East German sports system offered elite facilities and competitive infrastructure. She and her coach briefly fled to West Germany in 1958 but were forced back by the Stasi, creating a period of suspension and adversity.
starting_point: Born Karin Richert in Magdeburg, East Germany; competed in track and field events from her teens in the East German sports system.
current_position: Died on December 17, 2019 at age 81; final role: retired Olympic champion hurdler.

trajectory.event: Qualified for and competed at the Rome Olympics in the 80m hurdles, finishing fourth in her semifinal.
Won silver in the 80m hurdles at the European Athletics Championships.
Won Olympic gold in the 80m hurdles at the Tokyo Olympics, tying the world record.

name: Michel Ancel
milestone_by_age_26: Directed and designed Rayman, released in 1995 for PlayStation and other platforms at age 23.
early_history_summary: Showed early talent in computer animation, joined Ubisoft as a graphic artist at age 17, published his first game (Brain Blasters) at 18 in 1990, and began working on Rayman in 1992, which launched in 1995.
family_context_summary: Born in Monaco in 1972; father's military career caused the family to travel internationally during his early years, exposing him to video games in Tunisia before settling in France.
primary_early_advantage_tags: early game industry, Ubisoft recruitment, programming skills, mentor, international exposure
evidence_summary: Ancel showed early talent in computer animation and game design, creating a demo that attracted Ubisoft's attention at age 16-17. He joined Ubisoft as a graphic artist at 17 and published his first game (Brain Blasters) at 18 in 1990. By age 23, he directed Rayman (1995), which became a major franchise. His father's military career exposed him to international environments, and he discovered video games in Tunisia. The early video game industry in France, particularly Ubisoft's growth, provided a frontier ecosystem for his talents.
starting_point: Born in Monaco; father's military career caused the family to travel internationally, exposing him to video games in Tunisia before settling in France.
current_position: Retired video game designer; left Ubisoft in 2020 after a career spanning three decades; created the Rayman and Beyond Good & Evil franchises.

name: Itzhak Perlman
milestone_by_age_26: Won the prestigious Leventritt Competition in 1964 at age 19, leading to a burgeoning worldwide concert career.
early_history_summary: Showed extraordinary musical talent from age 3, contracted polio at age 4, studied at the Academy of Music in Tel Aviv, appeared on the Ed Sullivan Show at 13, then studied at Juilliard under Ivan Galamian and Dorothy DeLay before winning the Leventritt Competition at 19.
family_context_summary: Born in Tel Aviv in 1945 to Chaim Perlman, a barber, and Shoshana Perlman; parents emigrated to Israel separately in the 1930s; contracted polio at age 4 leaving his legs paralyzed.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources. Father was a barber, not a musician.
primary_early_advantage_tags: child prodigy, Juilliard, polio adversity, scholarships, elite training, perfect pitch
evidence_summary: Perlman showed extraordinary musical talent from age 3, requesting a violin after hearing one on the radio. He contracted polio at age 4, which paralyzed his legs but did not diminish his musical determination. He studied at the Academy of Music in Tel Aviv and was discovered in a talent search, leading to his Ed Sullivan Show appearance at 13 in 1958. He then studied at Juilliard under Ivan Galamian and Dorothy DeLay, winning the Leventritt Competition in 1964 at age 19. His parents, a barber and a homemaker, supported his training with scholarships from the America-Israel Cultural Foundation.
starting_point: Born in Tel Aviv in 1945 to Chaim Perlman, a barber, and Shoshana Perlman; contracted polio at age 4, leaving his legs paralyzed.
current_position: Renowned violinist and conductor; continues to perform and teach; 15-time Grammy Award winner; cultural icon in classical music.

trajectory.event: Appeared on the Ed Sullivan Show, propelling him to national recognition in the United States.

He won an award at the European Jazz Festival in Antibes and moved through several jazz bands (Second Roman New Orleans Jazz Band, the Flippers) before making his solo recording debut in 1964 at age 21. His first album '1999' was released in 1966. The Bologna jazz scene and band collaborations provided his early ecosystem, though his early solo work was commercially unsuccessful.
starting_point: Born in Bologna, Italy; mother gifted him a clarinet at age 13, sparking his musical career in the local jazz scene.
current_position: Died on March 1, 2012 at age 68; final role: iconic Italian singer-songwriter and musician.
